Let the real numbers $\mathrm{a}_1, \mathrm{a}_2 \ldots, \mathrm{a}_{50}$ be in an arithmetic progression. If $f\left(\mathrm{a}_{31}\right)=64 f\left(\mathrm{a}_{25}\right)$, and $\sum_{i=1}^{50} f\left(a_i\right)=3\left(2^{25}+1\right)$ then the value of $\sum_{i=6}^{30} f\left(a_i\right)$ is ________
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \because f(x+y)=f(x) \cdot f(y) \\ & \Rightarrow f(x)=k^x \quad(f(x)>0 \forall x \in R) \\ & \because f\left(a_{31}\right)=64 f\left(a_{25}\right)\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}^{(\mathrm{a}+30 \mathrm{ d})}=64 \cdot \mathrm{k}^{(\mathrm{a}+24 \mathrm{ d})} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}^{6 \mathrm{ d}}=64 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}^{\mathrm{d}}=2\end{aligned} \sum_{\mathrm{i}=1}^{50} \mathrm{f}\left(\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{i}}\right)=\mathrm{f}\left(\mathrm{a}_1\right)+\mathrm{f}\left(\mathrm{a}_2\right)+\ldots \ldots+\mathrm{f}\left(\mathrm{a}_{50}\right) \begin{aligned} & =\mathrm{k}^{\mathrm{a}}+\mathrm{k}^{\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{d}}+\ldots+\mathrm{k}^{\mathrm{a}+49 \mathrm{ d}}=\frac{\mathrm{k}^{\mathrm{a}}\left(\mathrm{k}^{50 \mathrm{ d}}-1\right)}{\mathrm{k}^{\mathrm{d}}-1} \\ & =\mathrm{k}^{\mathrm{a}}\left(2^{50}-1\right)=3\left(2^{25}+1\right)(\text{ Given }) \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}^{\mathrm{a}}=\frac{3}{2^{25}-1}\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & \therefore \sum_{\mathrm{i}=6}^{30} \mathrm{f}\left(\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{i}}\right)=\mathrm{k}^{\mathrm{a}+5 \mathrm{ d}}+\mathrm{k}^{\mathrm{a}+6 \mathrm{ d}}+\ldots+\mathrm{k}^{\mathrm{a}+29 \mathrm{ d}} \\ & \quad=\mathrm{k}^{\mathrm{a}+5 \mathrm{ d}} \frac{\left(\mathrm{k}^{25 \mathrm{ d}}-1\right)}{\mathrm{k}^{\mathrm{d}}-1}=\mathrm{k}^{\mathrm{a}} \cdot\left(\mathrm{k}^{\mathrm{d}}\right)^5\left(2^{25}-1\right) \\ & \quad=\frac{3}{2^{25}-1} \cdot 2^5\left(2^{25}-1\right)=96\end{aligned}$

Given,

$S = 77 + 757 + 7557 + \ldots + \overset{98}{7\overset{⏞}{5 \ldots 5}7}$

$⇒ S = 7 \times 10 + 7 + 7 \times 100 + 5 \times 10 + 7 + 7 \times 1000 + 5 \times 100 + 5 \times 10 + 7 \ldots + \overset{98}{7\overset{⏞}{5 \ldots 5}7}$

$⇒ S = 7\left(10 + {10}^{2} + \ldots + {10}^{99}\right) + 50\left(1 + 11 + \ldots + \overset{98}{\overset{⏞}{111 \ldots 1}}\right) + 7 \times 99$

$⇒ S = 70\left(\dfrac{{10}^{99} - 1}{9}\right) + \dfrac{50}{9}\left[\left(10 - 1\right) + \left({10}^{2} - 1\right) + \ldots + \left({10}^{98} - 1\right)\right] + 7 \times 99$

$⇒ S = 70\left(\dfrac{{10}^{99} - 1}{9}\right) + \dfrac{50}{9}\left[10\left(\dfrac{{10}^{98} - 1}{9}\right) - 98\right] + 7 \times 99$

$⇒ S = \dfrac{7 \times {10}^{100}}{9} - \dfrac{70}{9} + \dfrac{50}{9}\left[\dfrac{{10}^{99} - 1 - 9}{9} - 98\right] + 7 \times 99$

$⇒ S = \dfrac{7 \times {10}^{100}}{9} - \dfrac{70}{9} + \dfrac{50}{9}\left[\overset{99}{\overset{⏞}{111 \ldots 1}} - 99\right] + 7 \times 99$

$⇒ S = \dfrac{7 \times {10}^{100} - 70 + \overset{99}{\overset{⏞}{555 \ldots 5}}0}{9} - 550 + 693$

$⇒ S = \dfrac{7\overset{99}{\overset{⏞}{55 \ldots 5}}7 + 1210}{9}$

So, on comparing we get, $m + n = 1210 + 9 = 1219$

questions.q: Let ${a}_{1}, {a}_{2}, {a}_{3}, \ldots$ be an arithmetic progression with ${a}_{1} = 7$ and common difference $8$. Let ${T}_{1}, {T}_{2}, {T}_{3}, \ldots$ be such that ${T}_{1} = 3$ and ${T}_{n + 1} - {T}_{n} = {a}_{n}$ fo $n \ge 1$. Then, which of the following is/are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Given,

${a}_{n} = 7 + \left(n - 1\right)8$ and ${T}_{1} = 3$

Also ${T}_{n + 1} = {T}_{n} + {a}_{n}$

Now ${T}_{n} = {T}_{n - 1} + {a}_{n - 1}$

Putting $n = 1$ we get,

${T}_{2} = {T}_{1} + {a}_{1}$

Now putting $n = 2$ we get,

${T}_{3} = {T}_{2} + {a}_{2} ⇒ {T}_{3} = {T}_{1} + {a}_{1} + {a}_{2}$

And so on we get,

$⇒ {T}_{n + 1} = {T}_{1} + {a}_{1} + {a}_{2} + \ldots + {a}_{n}$

$⇒ {T}_{n + 1} = {T}_{1} + \dfrac{n}{2}\left[2\left(7\right) + \left(n - 1\right)8\right]$

$⇒ {T}_{n + 1} = {T}_{1} + n\left(4n + 3\right) ⋯ \left(1\right)$

Now for $n = 19$ we get,

${T}_{20} = 3 + \left(19\right)\left(79\right) = 1504$

And for $n = 29$ we get,

${T}_{30} = 3 + \left(29\right)\left(119\right) = 3454$ {option C is correct}

Now finding sum we get,

$\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{20}{T}_{k} = 3 + \mathop{∑}_{k = 2}^{20}{T}_{k} = 3 + \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{19}\left(3 + 4{n}^{2} + 3n\right)$

$= 3 + 3\left(19\right) + \dfrac{3\left(19\right)\left(20\right)}{2} + \dfrac{4\left(19\right)\left(20\right)\left(39\right)}{6}$

$= 3 + 10507 = 10510$ {option B is correct}

And Similarly $\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{30}{T}_{k} = 3 + \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{29}\left(4{n}^{2} + 3n + 3\right) = 35615$

questions.q: Let $AP\left(a; d\right)$ denote the set of all the terms of an infinite arithmetic progression with first term a and common difference $d > 0 .$ If $AP\left(1; 3\right) ∩ AP\left(2; 5\right) ∩ AP\left(3; 7\right) = AP\left(a; d\right)$ then $a + d$ equals ____
questions.solution:
Let ${T}_{\left(1, m\right)}: {m}^{th}$ term of ${1}^{st}$ series $A\left(1; 3\right)$
${T}_{\left(2, n\right)}: {n}^{th}$ term of ${2}^{nd}$ series $A\left(2; 5\right)$
${T}_{\left(3, r\right)}: {r}^{th}$ term of ${3}^{rd}$ series $A ( 3; 7 )$
For common terms
${T}_{( 1, m )} = {T}_{( 2, n )} = {T}_{( 3, r )}$
$1 + 3\left(m - 1\right) = 2 + 5\left(n - 1\right) = 3 + 7\left(r - 1\right)$
$3m - 2 = 5n - 3 = 7r - 4$
$⇒ m = \dfrac{5n - 1}{3}andr = \dfrac{5n + 1}{7}$
For $‘m’$ to be a natural number $n = 2,5, 11, \ldots$
And for $‘r’$ to be a natural number $n = 4,11, \ldots$
When $n = 11, m = 18 and r = 8$
$⇒$ For ${1}^{st}$ common term of three series $A ( a, d )$
$a = {1}^{st}$ term of $A ( 1,3 )$
$a = 1 + ( 181 ) 3 = 52$
$⇒$ Common difference of $A\left(a, d\right) = LCM$ of common difference of $\left(A\left(1; 3\right), A\left(2; 5\right), A\left(3; 7\right)\right)$
$d = LCM ( 3, 5, 7 )$
$d = 105$
Hence, $a + d = 52 + 105 = 157$

Let three sides of triangle be: $a - d, a, a + d$.

$⇒ a\left(a - 4d\right) = 0$

$⇒ a\left(a - d\right) = 48$        .....(ii)

$∴$     From (i) and (ii), we get  $a = 8, d = 2$

$\left(a - d\right) = \left(8 - 2\right) = 6$units

questions.solution:
We have, $S_k=\frac{\frac{k-1}{k !}}{1-\frac{1}{k}}=\frac{1}{(k-1) !}$
Now,

$\begin{aligned}$& $\left($k^2-3 k+1\right) S_k=\{(k-2)(k-1)-1\} \\
& =$\frac{1}{(k-3) !}-\frac{1}{(k-1) !}$\\
& \Rightarrow \sum_{k=1}^{100}$\left|\left($k^2-3 k+1\right) S_k\right| \\
& =1+1+2-$\left(\frac{1}{99 !}+\frac{1}{98 !}\right)=$4-$\frac{100^2}{100 !}
\end{aligned}

\Rightarrow \quad \frac{100^2}{100 !}+\sum_{k=1}^{100}\left|\left($k^2-3 k+1\right) S_k\right|=4

options:

$\frac{n\left(4 n^2+1\right) c^2}{3}$

$\frac{n\left(4 n^2-1\right) c^2}{3}$

$\frac{n\left(4 n^2+1\right) c^2}{6}$
questions.solution:
Let $S_n=c^2\begin{aligned}$& S_{n-1}=c(n-1)^2=c n²+c-2 c n \\

& T_n^2=(2 c n-c)^2=4 c² n²+c²-4 c² n \\
& \therefore $\text{ Sum }=\Sigma$T_n^2=$\frac{4 c^2 \cdot n(n+1)(2 n+1)}{6}$\\
& =$\frac{2 c^2 n(n+1)(2 n+1)+3 n c^2-6 c^2 n(n+1)}{3}$\\
& =$\frac{n c^2\left[4 n^2+6 n+2+3-6 n-6\right]}{3}$\\
& =$\frac{n c^2\left(4 n^2-1\right)}{3}
\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}$ n & =1,  $\frac{3}{4}$& < $\frac{1}{6}$ \\
n & =3, & $\frac{27}{64}$ & < $\frac{1}{6}$ \\
n & =5, & $\frac{243}{1024}$ & >$\frac{1}{6}
\end{aligned}$ which is true for $n=7$.
Obviously, $n_0=7$
